text: Dingaa Bunnits are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Bunnit family, and can be found at level 43 on the Great Sword's Hilt.
Detox Rhanas are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Rhana family, and can be found at level 58-59 at Cape Arcaphor in Erythia Sea.
Discordant Merignas are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Merigna family, and can be found at level 45 & 74 in Erythia Sea.
Demise Thrust (Japanese: ) is a Talent Art in . It is the Talent Art of the Thaumaturge class. The user readies their staff then extends it hard to pierce enemies.
Detonating Hit (Japanese: , Detonēshonhitto, Lit. "Detonation Hit") is a Battle Art in and . __TOC__
Destructive Charge is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Martial Artist class.
The Dome of Stahl (Japanese: , Sutaru no Daiengai) is a location in , located behind the Colony 4 Ferronis in the Eagus Wilderness.
The Desert Caravan is a shop in . It is run by a Traderpon and can be found at the Desert Ferronis Hulk in Dannagh Desert after completing The Desert Hulk.
Dirty Army Satchels are Collectible items in . They can be found in Origin.

Demnd Anloods (Japanese: , Demondo Haindo) are Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Anlood family, and can be found at level 44-45 at Elsayer Cape and in the Valley of Anguish on Rae-Bel Tableland.
Desert Paguls are Normal Minor Enemies in . They are members of the Pagul family, and can be found at level 44-46 in Erythia Sea.
Dig is a Battle Art in . It is one of the initial arts of the Soulhacker class.
Double Bite is a Battle Art in . It is one of the initial arts of the Soulhacker class.
The Depriti Pippito is a Quest Exclusive Boss in . It is a member of the Pippito family, and is fought at level 58 at Predator's Paw in Erythia Sea during Unspeakable Being.
Divine Protection (Japanese: ) is a Battle Art in . It is one of the arts of the Thaumaturge class.

Disparre Skwarors (Japanese: , Disupea Sutora, lit. Despair Skwaror) are DLC Quest Exclusive Enemies in . They are members of the Skwaror family, with three being encountered at level 20 on Ypsil Hill in Dannagh Desert during Champion of the Nopon.

Double Jeopardy is a Time Attack Challenge Battle in . It can be received from Nopon Archsage in the Land of Challenge, available as downloadable content from the second part of the Expansion Pass. Clearing this challenge with at least an A rank for the first time will unlock the Swimwear B outfit for Lanz.

Dino Storm is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Blazing Karlos while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.

Dino Flash is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Fineblade Faltaar while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.

Desperate Charge is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster King Krawkin while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.

Double Slap (Japanese: ) is a Battle Art in . It is an art of the Soulhacker class. It is acquired by defeating the Unique Monster Saberly Dorampé while the Soul Hack skill is set on any player-controlled party member.
Demonfang Necklaces are DLC Accessories in . They can be purchased from Prize X-change Blue in the Land of Challenge for 6000 Noponstones.
The Diablada Cliffs (Japanese: , Diaburāda Dangai) are a location in , located on the Aurora Shelf. This is where the party meets Shulk and Rex, and where they face Consul W.
Detonating Wave (Japanese: ) is one of Na'el's arts in . She moves back and launches a large blast of explosive energy at an enemy.
Doodlenoodles Recipe is a Key Item in . It allows the party to cook Legendary Doodlenoodles at Rest Spots.
The Desperate Agnian (Japanese: ) is a Boss in . She is an Agnus Soldier fought at level 6 alongside the Desperate Kevesi in Vermilion Woods. She is later revealed to be Glimmer.
The Desperate Kevesi (Japanese: ) is a Boss in . He is a Keves Soldier fought at level 6 alongside the Desperate Agnian in Vermilion Woods. He is later revealed to be Nikol.
The Disciples are an organization in . They are also known as Lord Zanza's Disciples or the Trinity.

Disappearing World is a Field Track from , composed by ACE. It is track twelve of disc five from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack. The song plays on the Lower Level of the First Low Orbit Station and in Elysium after the party meets the Architect. This song also plays when Mikhail tells Akhos and Patroka to go help Jin and Malos, before transforming the Marsanes into a mech to fight Indol.

Desolation is a track from , composed by ACE. It is track three of disc three from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track three of disc eight from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. This song plays during the following moments: * Rex and Mythra defeating Malos and Akhos at the Olethro Ruins. * The party gives their respects to Vandham at his grave. * Tatazo stopping Poppi from finishing off Lila, who then frees herself from Bana's control over her. * Niall's death and subsequent resurrection by Nia on the Titan Battleship in Indol. * Rex convincing Jin to stand down following the battle against him on the World Tree. * Amalthus's last stand, but is halted by Jin, who enco
Discussions are a mechanic in . They are somewhat reminiscent of Campsite chats from .
Dematerialization (English dub: ), or De-mat for short, is a phenomenon that occurs in .
Dorara is an NPC in . He is a Nopon who can be found at Goetuis Wharf #1 in the Indoline Praetorium during Chapter 6. He must be talked to when the party sets off for Tantal for the first time.

Doraram is an NPC in . He is a Nopon who appears in the Wrecc Marshland in the Gormott Province during The Ties That Bind. He is part of the Gormott branch of a cult known as the "Harbingers of Eschapon", and attempts to perform a ceremony in order to summon a Nopon demon prince. However, a Ravenous Arachno is summoned instead. He is unable to be spoken to.
Diskbombs are sidearms for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Spine-Cannon/E-Bubble/B-Bomb types Qmoevas or female Milsaadi.

Dunban (Japanese: , Danban; English dub: ) is a Homs, and is one of the seven playable characters in . Dunban serves as the voice of reason for the group, willing to kill a Homs in order to bring peace. Dunban owns a house in Colony 9 where he lives with his younger sister Fiora. Riki calls him "Dundun". He is initially playable in the Prologue and Chapter 2 as a guest character and he becomes permanently playable during Chapter 5.

Eks Iron Hearts (Japanese: , Ekusu no Tetsu Shinzō) are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be dropped by Eks in Makna Forest, or traded for in Frontier Village. According to their description, the taste of them is great, but jaws of steel are needed to eat them. Two are needed for The Melody of Happiness, and one for the reconstruction of Colony 6. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 1,700 Noponstones.

Dust Elements are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from Caris Nebula in Makna Forest and by trading with Hoko before he moves to Colony 6 from Frontier Village. According to their description, they are dust elements that cause a dust storm if dropped in a sandy place. Two are required for Colony 6 Reconstruction. In Definitive Edition, they can be purchased in Time Attack place from Nopon Archsage for 3,000 Noponstones.

Désirée (Japanese: , Dejirēn) is a Homs in . She can be found wandering around the northern part of the Commercial District in Colony 9 at night. It is heavily implied that she is the daughter of Xord.

Earnest (Japanese: , Ōnesuto) is a Homs in . He can be found at the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg. It is revealed during Earnest's Solitude that he had a friend who was killed by an Arrogant Tirkin near Kasharpa Falls.

Dramatic Nights (Japanese: , Yamiyo Doramachikku) are collectables in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be found in Agniratha and later in Colony 6. According to their description, Reyn was serious when he named them and they look like dangerous-looking components.
Eiz (Japanese: , Ain) is a Machina in Xenoblade Chronicles. He feels partly responsible for what Egil did, and buries remains to try to forget. He can be found outside the Hidden Machina Village.

Education-Minded Suzanna (Japanese: , Kyōiku Nesshin'na Suzanna) is a quest in . It can be received from Suzanna dwelling west of the Residential District of Colony 9, southwest of Tranquil Square. After this quest is completed, Suzanna may offer another quest, Education-Crazy Suzanna. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment.

Education-Crazy Suzanna (Japanese: , Kyōiku Kajōna Suzanna) is a quest in . It can be received from Suzanna dwelling west of the Residential District of Colony 9, southwest of Tranquil Square. After this quest is completed, Kantz may offer another quest, Birthday Shoes. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment.

Earnest's Fibs (Japanese: , Usotsuki Ōnesuto) is a quest in . It can be received from Earnest in the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg. It is the first in a series of three quests that Earnest can give. If Reyn is in the active party, he will comment. After completing this quest, Earnest may offer Earnest's Mischief.

Dulland (Japanese: , Dyurando) is a Homs in . He can first be found at the Main Entrance of Colony 6 if the Colony has not yet begun its reconstruction by the time the party meets Miqol in the Hidden Village. Once the colony has begun reconstruction and after the events in the Mechonis Core, he stands by the bridge from Junks to the Colony 6 lake, close to the Reconstruction HQ. Later, he relocates to the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg. Once all of his quests have been completed, he can be found sitting in Outlook Park in Colony 9, with an unnamed High Entia woman.
Duel Guarder (Japanese: , Dyuerugādā) is a weapon in . It is one of Reyn's gunlances.

Electric Crickets (Japanese: , Shidenkoorogi) are collectables in . They can be found in Agniratha and Colony 6. According to their description, they are capable of firing thunderbolts but the effort leaves them dazed and immobile.

Dynamite are Key Items in . They can be found in the Ether Mine. There are three of them, and they must be obtained for Making a New Path in Colony 6. When they are delivered to Gorman, he will use them to blow open a new path at Spiral Valley on Bionis' Leg, making it possible to complete For the Restoration without defeating the monster blocking the path. On the Ether Mine map: * One is south of the "2" in "Test Pit 2" in a dead end. * One is in the dead end just south of "Test Pit 3" (due south of the "t" in "Pit"). * One is slightly to the east of the "4" in "Test Pit 4".

Eks (Japanese: , Ekusu, lit. Equus) are a family of horse or unicorn-like enemies in the . They are structurally similar to Bargs, and slightly similar to Ponios, which are also horse-like. There is a large appearance change between the games; Eks in and are less spiny, rounder and more horse-like than Eks in .

The Eks Watering Hole (Japanese: , Ekusu no Mizunomiba) is a location in . It is a large series of pools in Makna Forest, just west of Twisted Tree Gate and north of the path that leads down to Sparkling Pool. There is a Heart-to-Heart here - "Riki's Crazy Crystal Plan" - and an Earth Ether Deposit.

Dunban's House (Japanese: , Danban-tei) is a location in . It is located in Colony 9. It is found to the side of the bridge at the Main Entrance, in the Commercial District. It is where Dunban and Fiora live. There is a Heart-to-Heart inside - "Fiora's Cooking" - between Fiora and Reyn.
Dyed Mules are light feet armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be worn by female party members.
Dyed Bottoms are light legs armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be worn by female party members.
Dyed Tops are light torso armour in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can only be worn by female party members.
Eclipse Armour is heavy torso armour in . It is made with lost technology left by the Machina.
Eclipse Leggings are heavy legs armour in . They can be dropped by Throne Sardi.

Earnest's Solitude (Japanese: , Kodoku no Ōnesuto) is a quest in . It can be received from Earnest in the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg. It is the third and final quest in a series of three quests given by Earnest, and involves placing flowers on the grave of Earnest's friend by Kasharpa Falls. If Sharla is in the active party, she will comment.
Eclipse Gauntlets are heavy arms armour in . They are made with technology left by the Machina.

Dynastrars (Japanese: , Dainasutā) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are gunlances wielded by Reyn, and can be obtained from various low-level enemies. They can also be purchased from the Syrath Lighthouse Shop shop.
Draft Rifles (Japanese: , Dorafutoraifuru) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are ether rifles wielded by Sharla.

Dream Gnashers (Japanese: , Yumemi no Tsukutsuku) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are biters wielded by Riki. They can be acquired by trading with Galdo or Arielle whom can be found in Alcamoth as well as trading with Talonyth who can be found in Colony 6.
Dystopia (Japanese: , Disutopia) are weapons in . They are Fiora's twin blades with the highest displayed average Attack value.

Dragon Rod Alcar (Japanese: , Ryūjō Arukatorazu, Dragon Rod Alcatraz) is a weapon in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a staff wielded by Melia. The core of the staff is a talon from the Dragon King Alcar. It can only be obtained from a Giants' Treasure Chest in a hidden room of the Central Hall.
Dusk Staves (Japanese: , Dasukusutaffu) are weapons in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are staves wielded by Melia. They can only be obtained from a single shop.

Earnest's Mischief (Japanese: , Hitodenashi Ōnesuto) is a quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Earnest in the Refugee Camp on Bionis' Leg. It is the second in a series of three quests given by Earnest. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment. After this quest, Earnest may offer Earnest's Solitude.

Elder Gragus (Japanese: , Rōkei no Guragūsu) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Quadwing family, and can be found at level 34 on high ground east of the Nopon Arch in Makna Forest. The Elder Gragus must be defeated in order to complete the The Old Soldier's Test quest. It can drop an All-Seeing Eye, three of which are needed for Secret Elixir Ingredients.

Drizzle Elements are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles. They can be obtained from two types of Nebulae and Flabbergasted Jerome in Eryth Sea and Makna Forest, or traded for with Miko in Frontier Village. According to their description, they are water elements that cause a shower of drizzle within a fifty centimeter radius.
EXP Up (Japanese: , EXP Appu) is a Gem in and that increases the amount of EXP gained by defeating enemies. __TOC__
The Dull Radiant is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is one of the four Radiants required for Ancient Ceremony Offerings. It can be found at the Dark Swamp in Satorl Marsh.

Electric Plus (Japanese: , Kaminari Kyōka) is a Gem in that increases damage dealt by electric attacks. This Gem should not be confused with Lightning Attack, a Gem type which allows auto-attacks to deal electric damage. __TOC__
Earth Cloak (Japanese: , Chijō Meisai) is a Gem in that reduces the detection range of ground enemies. __TOC__

Drive Boost (Japanese: , Doraibu Būsuto) is one of Sharla's arts in . It activates an aura that reduces the Cooldown time for her other arts. She cannot move or Auto-Attack while the Drive Boost aura is active. In , Kino has an identical version of this art called B-B-B-Boost.
Electric Gutbuster (Japanese: , Raijin Hōkyaku) is one of Dunban's physical arts in . When it is used after Gale Slash, it may inflict Break on an enemy.

※ After this quest is completed, Betty may offer Betty's Gift if the A route was taken or Désirée may offer Désirée's Apology if the B route was taken. Désirée's Future (Japanese: , Dejirēn no Shōrai) is a quest in . It can be received from Désirée north of the Commercial District of Colony 9. This quest will be available once Satorl Marsh is accessible, meaning the Ether Mine events cleared with Xord defeated, as occurs a special one-of-a-kind conversation with Désirée about her father who was a fine blacksmith killed in the Battle of Sword Valley. After this conversation about her father, it is also required to have completed the quest Jackson's Awakening, to have a Colony 9 affinity of ☆4

Drones (Japanese: , Furappu) are Mechonis equipment in . They are listed under the "Feet" tab in the in-game inventory, but are shown to be worn on the back. They can only be worn by Fiora, and determine what Talent Art she will have. Her default talent art is Cannon Drones I if no drones are worn. The following tables show the list of drones equipment and the stats for each talent art.

The Drainage Outlet (Japanese: , Koroni 6 Haisuiguchi) is a landmark in . It is located in Colony 6, south of the Splintered Path. It is the only entrance to the Ether Mine, which are accessed through the sewers. When it is raining, Water Upas appear just outside the mines.
Drifter Jutard (Japanese: , Meisō no Shutādo) is a Unique Monster in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is a member of the Hox family, and can be found at level 25 at the Pod Depot in Colony 6.

Duel Ignas are enemies in . They are members of the Igna family, and can be found at levels 21 - 24 northeast of the Crown Tree and in the Igna Territory in Satorl Marsh. They can drop the Igna Stone Pots needed for Nopon Determination.

Ekidno Jaw Gristle is a rare material in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is dropped by various Ekidno at Eryth Sea, and can be traded for. According to their description, they are considered a bizarre Nopon delicacy that tastes amazing with fried rice. Five are needed for Getting Bigger!.
The Drainage Control Room (Japanese: , Haisui Seigyo-shitsu) is a landmark in . It is located in the Ether Mine. There is a shop and two Nopon Merchants inside the control room.

Eater Caterpiles (Japanese: , Īto Kyapiru) are caterpillar-like enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles. They are members of the Caterpile family, and can be found in the Caterpile Nest in Tephra Cave. They drop Caterpile Poison, five lots of which is needed if following Leopold's branch in the quest Financial Planning.

Désirée's Apology (Japanese: , Dejirēn no Shazai) is a quest in . It can be received from Désirée near the Gem Man's Stall in the Commercial District of Colony 9. This quest and Betty's Gift are mutually exclusive. If Dunban is in the active party, he will comment.

Easy Hox (Japanese: , Ījī Hoggusu) are enemies in . They are members of the Hox family, and can be found at level 14 on Bionis' Leg, on the cliffs northeast of Jabos Rock Rest Area and in the trees south of Kamos Guidepost. They can drop the Sharp Hox Spurs needed for Colony 6 Reconstruction.
Drunk Vangs (Japanese: , Doranku Vanpu) are enemies in . They are members of the Vang family, and can be found at levels 18-20 in the Ether Mine, near Test Pit 2 and east of Test Pit 4.

This quest will expire if the second objective of The Melody of Happiness is completed instead. Dream of a Poet (Japanese: , Muchū no Shijin, The Dreamy Poet) is a Timed Quest in Xenoblade Chronicles. It can be received from Yura south of the Armu Farm, leaning against the backside of the houses, in Colony 6. If Shulk is in the active party, he will comment. This quest and The Melody of Happiness are mutually exclusive.

The Drainage Tunnel (Japanese: , Chika Kōdō Haisuikuchi) is a landmark in . It is located on the ground floor of the Ether Mine. It is the first landmark accessed in the mines, being the entrance from the Drainage Outlet at Colony 6, and it leads to the Drainage Control Room. It is inhabited by Colony Upas and a single Drunk Vang.
Dunban's Right Arm (Japanese: , Danban no Migiude) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in a turret at Hope Farm in Colony 6, between Dunban and Sharla at purple affinity.
Echoes of Ancient Times (Japanese: , Kodai no Zanshi) is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located in the Valley of Emperors in the High Entia Tomb, between Reyn and Melia at green affinity.

Drifter is a Class featured in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is the base Class, being Cross's initial class. Drifter offers a balanced variety of Arts, but no stat bonuses. The standard equipped Weapons are Knives and Assault Rifles. Once the Class Rank reaches 10, this Class can be changed to more specialized Striker, Commando, or Enforcer. The basic Arts of the Drifter are Assault Hammer and Flame Grenade. Drifter has five Skill slots, though the class has no skills of its own.

Dual Swords are melee weapons in . They are used by Commandos and can be mastered through the Winged Viper and Full Metal Jaguar Classes. Dual Swords are also the melee weapons used by Elma, Phog, Murderess, and Neilnail.

Dual Guns are ranged weapons in . They are the ranged weapons for Commandos, and can be further mastered through the Winged Viper and Full Metal Jaguar Classes. Dual Guns are also the ranged weapons used by Elma, Phog, Celica, and Liesel.
Désirée's Watch is a Key Item in Xenoblade Chronicles. It is received during The Broken Watch when Désirée asks Shulk to repair it.

Duplicator Probes are types of Data Probes in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They copy the functions of other nearby Data Probes. They are known as Copy Probes in the Japanese version. By installing Duplicator Probes near probes like Research Probes or Storage Probes, they will make them mimic their function. For example by placing in intersection three Storage Probes and one Booster Probe, the effect of the Duplicator Probe will be worth 3 x 3000 Storage and also boost the three Storage Probes to contain even more Storage.

Duelist (known as General Sword in the Japanese version) is a Class featured in . This class provides bonuses to HP and melee attack. It is one of six final classes and can only be leveled up from Samurai Gunner. Nagi and Al's class is an Alternative Duelist called Duelist+. Duelist has three Skill slots. Mastering this class enables Cross to equip Assault Rifles and Longswords with any class.
Drum Roll is one of Lin's two Signature Arts in . It is a Melee Art acquired after completing the Affinity Mission To Serve Nopon.

Dozer is a Skell model in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is also known as Yumbo in the Japanese version. It is a level 30 Heavy Type Skell. Dozer is one of the Skells of the BLADE in New Los Angeles. It was part of Bozé's DLC in the Japanese version. The blueprints are unlocked as a reward for completing Bozé's final Affinity Mission Bozé's Ignorance.
Dual Dynamo is one of L's two Signature Arts in . Cross can learn it by completing The Nopon Heir.

The Drainage Control Room Shop is a shop in . It is the only shop in the Ether Mine. It consists of a Nopon Merchant in the upper levels of the mine. It has a good selection of arts manuals for Reyn and Sharla, as well as two for Shulk. __TOC__
Drone Mortifoles (Japanese: , Dorōn Foriumu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Mortifole family, and can be found at level 16-20 at Twin Arches in Oblivia.

The East Gate Plain (Japanese: , Īsuto Gēto no Heigen) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, being the field just outside New Los Angeles's East Gate. The East Gate BC can be found down the road from the gate. This area's segments are largely centered around FN Site 116.

The East Gate BC (Japanese: , Īsuto Gēto BC) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a BLADE base camp run by the Reclaimers located in Primordia, an the East Gate side of New Los Angeles. East Gate Plain is landmarked in this area.

Droll Saltats (Japanese: , Dorōru Sarutāto) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Saltat family, and can be found at level 22-29 at Janpath Lake, Biahno River, and Unicorn Rock in Primordia.
East Janpath Plain (Japanese: , Janpasu-ko no Higashi Heigen) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Primordia, east of Janpath Lake.

Durvin, the Perceptive (Japanese: , Keigan no Doruvan) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Sphinx family. It can be found at level 70 at the Beasts' Lair in Primordia during the day.
Eagle Eye is a Sniper Rifle Battle Art in . It increases party members' Ranged Accuracy and Attack.

Draw Melee is a Soul Voice in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is activated when a party member begins a battle using a Melee Weapon. Regardless of customization, the Soul Voice always requests a Melee Art.
Draw Ranged is a Soul Voice in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is triggered when a party member starts a battle using a Ranged Weapon.
East Melville Street (Japanese: , Mobīsutorīto Higashi) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles, east of Central Melville Street.

The Elder Grex (Japanese: , Erudā Rupusu) is a Main Boss in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Grex family. Cross and Elma fight it during the prologue at level 4 on West Gate Plain in Primordia, before Cross enters New Los Angeles for the first time. It is accompanied by the two Callow Grexes.

Dove Turbas (Japanese: , Davu Kurekusu) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Turba family, and can be found at level 11-15 at FN Site 222 and Rust Lake, level 18-20 at Waterway Tangle, and level 16-18 around the base of Everwhelm Falls in Noctilum.
Drone King Quos (Japanese: , Dorōnkingu Kuō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Ganglion Quos and can be found at level 55 in Jair Fortress in Oblivia.

Dusk Adseculas (Japanese: , Dasuku Apisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Adsecula family, and can be found in Primordia, at level 31-32 above Northpointe Beach and level 39-40 under a wishbone-shaped rock formation near FN Site 111 and west of FN Site 119. The lower-leveled variants are aggressive, while the higher-leveled ones are nonaggressive and can be trampled by a Skell.

Drone Adseculas (Japanese: , Dorōn Apisu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Adsecula family, and can be found at level 12-15 in the Devil's Colony in Oblivia. They are hidden on the walls.

Edgardo, the Carefree (Japanese: , Kyosei no Edogarudo) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Thallus family. It can be found at level 18 near North Coast in Oblivia. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Edgardo, the Carefree. This Tyrant is camouflaged as a tree, sticking out from the face of the third head looking structure on the beach from the probe. It can be provoked by running around in front of it.

Drongo Caravan (English dub: ) (Japanese: , Dorongo Kyaraban) is a landmark in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Nopon Caravan located in Cauldros north of the Scholes Battlegrounds. It must be visited during Hope Springs Eternal, My Angel, My Lana, Sparking a Smile and Unknown Assailant.
Echo Germivores (Japanese: , Ekō Burōsu) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Germivore family, and can be found at level 12-18 at Seabird's Beak in Sylvalum.
East Ciel Sandsea (Japanese: , Shieru-ko no Tōbu Sakai) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in Sylvalum, on the east side of Lake Ciel.

The Drowning Ring (Japanese: , Umi no An'noun Ringu, Marine Unknown Ring) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a ring structure located in Oblivia, southeast of the Azure Lagoon and on the western end of the South Coast. The Ringstone can be found here during Forbidden Love.
Drone Pawn Quos (Japanese: , Dorōnpōn Kuō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Ganglion Quos and can be found at level 11 or at level 17-18 in Cauldros, northwest of FN Site 505.
Drone Rook Quos (Japanese: , Dorōnrūku Kuō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Ganglion Quos and can be found at level 37-40 in Bedrock Hold in Primordia.
Drone Knight Quos (Japanese: , Dorōn'naito Kuō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Ganglion Quos and can be found at level 23-24 in Noctilum, northwest of FN Site 210.
Ejiri Promontory (Japanese: , Ejiri-misaki) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located in south Oblivia. FN Site 314 is on the far edge of the promontory.
Eddie's Conquest (Japanese: , Edo Borutekkusu, Ed Vortex) is an area in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a small open-topped hollow located in Oblivia, directly north and above the Twin Arches.
Echo Rocks (Japanese: , Hateshinaki Sakebi no Iwa) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia.
Earthfreezers (Japanese: , Āsufurīzā) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Noctilum.
Echo Thalluses (Japanese: , Ekō Arudare) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Thallus family, and can be found at level 11-20 at Canopied Nightwood in Noctilum.

Eddy, the Electric Heat (Japanese: , Dennetsu no Edī) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Scintimure family. It can be found at level 43 under Titan's Table in Cauldros. Defeating it is required to complete the eponymous Basic Mission Eddy, the Electric Heat.
Drums of Valor (Japanese: , Yūki no Taiko) are prime collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Oblivia, in the Beachside Trove. Nine of them are required for A Hero's Welcome.
Dring Slicks (Japanese: , Doringu no Ryūdo) are common collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Sylvalum.
Druid Papils (Japanese: , Doruido Papirio) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Papil family, and can be found at level 8-9 east of Seabird's Beak BC in Sylvalum at daytime.
Dryland Papils (Japanese: , Dorai Papirio) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Papil family, and can be found at level 32-40 at Abandoned Bivouac in Cauldros.
Dulcet Geese (Japanese: , Randamode) are unique collectibles in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be found in Cauldros.
Duoguill Broths are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Duoguills in Primordia or Oblivia.

Egg Blattas (Japanese: , Eggu Buratta) are enemies in . They are members of the Blatta family. They can be found at level 8-9 near East Gate Plain in Primordia during nighttime. The occassionally replace Nocto Blatta which are feeding on Suid corpses.
Elaine, the Lunar Eclipse (Japanese: , Gesshoku no Erein) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Ceto family. It can be found at level 55 at Lake Basel in Oblivia at night.

Drake, the Waypost (Japanese: , Dōhyō no Doreiku) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Caecus family. It can be found at level 29 in Noctilum in Orochi's Belly, where it guards a field treasure.
Dui, the Invaluable (Japanese: , Nekome no Tui) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Blatta family. It can be found at level 21-25 inside Devil's Colony in Oblivia.

Draken, the Drifting Cloud (Japanese: , Ukigumo no Doreikun) is a Tyrant in . It is a member of the Balaena family. It can be found at level 85 in the Primordia Waters. It is followed by a pair of Shoal Balaena, and attacking them will aggro it and vice versa.

Duran, the Draconian (Japanese: , Kikyōkan Dyuran) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Marnuck Ganglion member. It can be found at level 38 at the O'rrh Sim Castle Ruins in Cauldros at any time except late night. It is accompanied by Spaniel, the Obedient and a pair of Legion Caro.

Du-rha, the Imprisoned (Japanese: , Fūjirareshi Du-raa) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Xe-dom machine. It can be found at level 74 in Quay Hollows in Sylvalum. It is the only enemy that can drop Xe-dom Crimson Crests. Its arts include Arm Swing (physical), Mega Graviton (gravity), and Piercing Claw (electric).

Duran's Galdr (Japanese: , Dyuran Sen'yō Garudora) is a Tyrant in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a Galdr machine. It can be found at level 40 at Lotus Keep Building Site in Noctilum at late night. It is the Galdr of Duran, the Draconian.

Dysprosium Petramands (Japanese: , Jisupuroshiumu Aranea) are minor enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Petramand family, and can be found at level 35-36 around FN Site 505 and FN Site 506 in Cauldros. They can also be found at the Infernal Ledges.

Drifter Unafulges (Japanese: , Dorifuto Purumō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Unafulge family, and can be found at level 31-40 at the top of the waterfall by FN Site 207 in Noctilum during the night.

Dryland Unafulges (Japanese: , Dorai Purumō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Unafulge family, and can be found at level 36 at Samuel Incline, 31-32 at South Ciel Sandsea, level 34 at East Ciel Sandsea in Sylvalum, and at level 33-34 at North Ciel Sandsea.
ER001: Emeroa (Japanese: , ER001: Emeroa) is an NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Definian who appears in the Ganglion Antropolis in Cauldros during the Normal Mission Definian Downfall.
Dual Boards are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Pugiliths or Qmoevas.
Electric Flesh is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Astral Crusader at rank 9.
Electric Guard is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Partisan Eagle at rank 3.
Electric Boost is a Skill in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked as a Partisan Eagle at rank 5. Cross, Alexa, Lao and Bozé can use this skill.

Drone Queen Quos (Japanese: , Dorōnkuīn Kuō) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Ganglion Quos, and can be found at level 41-50 in Cauldros's O'rrh Sim Keep or northwest of FN Site 507 on Adder Byroad.

Duna Valdileo is a NPC in Xenoblade Chronicles X. She is a Tree Clan Prone and can be found at the Port Side of the Ma-non Ship in New Los Angeles during the day. She is Liana Valdileo's and Nemard Wolfen's sister and Auld Belgazus's granddaughter.

Ebony Evello Eggs are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from brown Evellos in Oblivia. They are components in rank I and V Antispike, Back Attack Plus, Spike.EVA, and PositionDmg.BACK augments. Two are needed for the Normal Mission Mayhem.

Duel Emperor Qmoevas (Japanese: , Dyueruenperā Kumūba) are enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are Qmoeva machines, and can be found at level 41-50 in the skies over Sunset Falls and T'phnom Shelf in Cauldros.

Driving Force is Elma's third Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located to the east of East Melville Street in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles, between Elma and Cross in the morning.

The Dryland Auravis (Japanese: , Dorai Akuira) is a Mission Exclusive Enemy in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a member of the Auravis family fought at level 35 at Qing Long Glade in Noctilum during No-show Nen'celeg.

Drinking Buddies is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located to the northwest of East Melville Street in the Commercial District of New Los Angeles, between Frye and Cross at any time.
Dragon's Maw! is a Heart-to-Heart in . It is located south of the BLADE Tower behind a tall structure in the Administrative District of New Los Angeles between Alexa and Cross in the morning.

Dulling the Pain is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located between the Repenta Diner and the Integrated Production Plant in the Industrial District of New Los Angeles between Frye and Cross at any time.
Eerie Lightning Tentacles are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from the Rexoskell. They are components in making several Skell Superweapons.
Electric-Flood is a superweapon for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It fills both shoulder slots. It is the only superweapon with a Debuff Art.
Dreamweavers is a Heart-to-Heart in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is located at the Water Purification Plant of the Residential District of New Los Angeles between Gwin and Cross at late night.
Duoguill Duty is a Basic Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is a request from the Dorian Caravan and the primary destination is Oblivia.

The Drone-Storm is a superweapon for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X. The level 60 schematic FILE-USP1080GG is obtained by completing the Affinity Mission Fathers and Sons. It is known as Disk-Flap in the Japanese version.
Dragoon Lance is a superweapon for Skells in Xenoblade Chronicles X.

Dune Adseculas (Japanese: , Dyūn Apisu) are Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are level 39 members of the Adsecula family. Three of them must be fought at Oblivia's Kintrees during A New Life. Their arts include Acid Bolt (electrical), Bolt Strike (electrical), and Flash (ether).
Dried Seaweed Lichens are common materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from Tectinsulas.

E.M. Units are rare materials in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They can be obtained from green Galdrs, or for 90 Reward Tickets at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks. They are components in X, XV, and XX Max HP Drive augments.

Drove Adseculas (Japanese: , Dorōbu Apisu) are three Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Adsecula family, and are fought at level 40 at Lake Ciel in Sylvalum during The Duel (Part III).
Duoguill A is a Holofigure in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It depicts a blue duoguill variant. It can be obtained from silver drops from Hephaestus, the Absconder in Primordia.
Duoguill B is a Holofigure in . It depicts a black duoguill variant. It can be obtained from silver drops from Valeriano, the Rolling Thunder in Oblivia.

Drifting Mortifoles is a Squad Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is part of BLADE Mission No.7, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting eight Unafulges. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Eerie Ecology is a Squad Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is part of BLADE Mission No.10, and is unlocked when the Squad has completed the Squad Task of hunting twenty Caecuses. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Dread Blattas (Japanese: , Doreddo Buratta) are Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Blatta family, and are fought at level 39 in the East Gate Plain of Primordia during route A of An Ancient Legend. Fifteen of them spawn initially, and they respawn approximately one minute after being killed. The party must defend against the onslaught for two minutes.

Dread Petramands (Japanese: , Doreddo Aranea) are Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Petramand family, and are fought at level 39 in the East Gate Plain of Primordia during route A of An Ancient Legend. Ten of them spawn initially, and they respawn approximately one minute after being killed. The party must defend against the onslaught for two minutes.

Dread Ciniculas (Japanese: , Doreddo Vasaruto) are Mission Exclusive Enemies in Xenoblade Chronicles X. They are members of the Cinicula family, and are fought at level 39 in the East Gate Plain of Primordia during route A of An Ancient Legend. Four of them spawn initially, and they respawn approximately one minute after being killed. The party must defend against the onslaught for two minutes.

Dynamic Nature is a Support Mission in Xenoblade Chronicles X. It is unlocked when Chapter 12 is completed. It allows the player to quickly raise affinity with party members, and earn Division Points to raise one's BLADE Level. Enemies do not drop any items in this mission. It can be accepted at the Network Console in the BLADE Barracks.

Driver Combos are battle mechanics in and . They consist of Driver Arts performed in a particular sequence. A Driver Combo begins when an Art inflicts Break on the enemy, after which it can be Toppled, then Launched and finally Smashed by using Arts with those effects before the enemy recovers. Toppling or Launching an enemy also produces a medium HP Potion, while Smashing an enemy produces a large HP Potion and causes the enemy to drop items such as Core Chips, Core Crystals, and Gold. Some Driver Arts, such as Rex's Mighty Ball and Brave Throw Bitball arts, have effects which further increases the damage dealt to Toppled or Launched enemies.
Dynamic Spark Sword (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when using the Big Bang Edge.
Dual Slash (Japanese: , De~yuarusurasshu) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when using a Chroma Katana.
Eightfold Edge (Japanese: , lit. Eight Edge) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Rex's arts when using Twin Rings.
Dried Sunfishs Seafood are Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Ikthus Fishmongers in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya. They are one of the favorite Pouch items of Dromarch.

The Elder Arachno (Japanese: , Erudā Supaido) is a Boss in . It is fought at level 22 atop Soulcrown Summit in the Kingdom of Uraya. It is both a member of the Arachno family and a Driver as it is accompanied by a Blade in battle, serving as an introduction to how large creatures, in particular among Unique Monsters, can drive Blades as well. In addition to two Common Core Crystals and one Rare Core Crystal, the Elder Arachno will drop the Beastly Core Crystal once it is defeated, from which its Blade, named Wulfric, can be resonated with.

The Dragon's Whiskers (Japanese: , Ryū no Hige) is a Secret Area in . It is located in the Head of the Kingdom of Uraya. It is accessible only by diving from a pond at the Cataracts of Rujah, and requires level 4 "Water Mastery" and "Fortitude" Field Skill. There are no enemies here.
Eight-Rock Skip (Japanese: , Kojō Hakkoku Tobi) is a landmark in . It is located in the middle of Bluestep Ditch in the Stomach of the Kingdom of Uraya. It consists of eight large rocks.

Drillbore Bridge (Japanese: , Senkō-bashi) is a location in . It is located in the Stomach of the Kingdom of Uraya, between Tardy Gate and the Stone Gate Ruins. Konakona can be found here prior to the DLC quest M.I.A. Nopon.

The Dragon's Stomach (Japanese: , Ryū no Ibukuro) is a location in . It is located in the Head of the Kingdom of Uraya, to the north of Cataracts of Rujah. It is infested by Parisax, including the Unique Monster Vampire Bride Marion. This place is initially sealed and first accessed during the quest The Titan Scholar.
Eaux de Doux are Cosmetic Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Cleo's Cosmetics in Goldmouth in the Argentum Trade Guild.
Elastifying Tonics are Cosmetic Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Cleo's Cosmetics in the Argentum Trade Guild. They are one of Fiora's favorite Pouch Items.
Dueling Kingdoms are Board Game Pouch items in . They can be purchased from Elgeschel Hobby Store in Alba Cavanich in the Empire of Mor Ardain.
Duel Lines are Board Game Pouch items in . They can be purchased at Hobby Knick-Knacks in Fonsa Myma in the Kingdom of Uraya.
Dyphne is an NPC in . Dyphne is a Tantalese who can be found in the Kingdom of Tantal's Theosoir. Dyphne runs a shop called Praximo Cosmetics specialized in Cosmetics.

Drifting Soul is an event track in , composed and arranged by ACE, with original lyrics by Tetsuya Takahashi, English translation by LYSSA and Castro Satoshi, and vocals by Jen Bird. It is track nineteen of disc two from the Xenoblade 2 Original Soundtrack, and track nineteen of disc seven from the Xenoblade Original Soundtrack Trinity Box. The song plays when the party struggles against Malos and Akhos in the Olethro Ruins, and during the cutscene after the first phase of the final battle against Artifice Aion, when Rex tries to get through to Malos, while the Architect realizes that the demise of his other half is imminent. Drum Gogols (Japanese: , Doramu Gogōru) are enemies in . They are members of the Gogol family and can be found at level 11-13 on the Upper Level - Right area of the Gormott Province, particularly on the Plains of Evening Calm.

Eggle Jetty (Abandoned) (Japanese: , Eguru Haisanbashi) is a location in . It is located on the Lower Level of the Empire of Mor Ardain, near the two west Salvage Points. It can be accessed by traveling to the Fourth Ridge Entrance and heading south along the walkways. It is directly beside the Abandoned Excavation. There is a Treasure Trove here containing two Common Core Crystals and gold.

Dynal Gyannas (Japanese: , Dainamu Gyanomu) are enemies in . They are members of the Gyanna family, and can be found at level 37 - 41 at the Hope's Horizon on the Upper Level of the Kingdom of Tantal.
Drux Tirkin (Japanese: , Dorukusu Tākin) are enemies in . They are members of the Tirkin family, and can be found at level 81-84 at the Old Gelgemos Gate on the Lower Level of the Kingdom of Tantal.

Eanl Blants (Japanese: , Iyanru Barando) are enemies in . They are members of the Blant family, and can be found at level 45-47 at the Wonder Spring Plaza Ruins on the Mid Level of the Spirit Crucible Elpys. Dusky Riiks (Japanese: , Dasukyi Ratōru) are enemies in . They are members of the Riik family, and can be found at level 44-46 at the uppermost level of the Wonder Spring Plaza Ruins on the Mid Level of the Spirit Crucible Elpys. Four spawn behind the Elpys Great Hall on the way toward the Wonder Spring Plaza Ruins. They climb down from the walls of dead ends when the player comes close. Three of them must be defeated during the quest Difficult Decisions. Five of them must be defeated to unlock Theory's level 2 "Ice Mastery", Dahlia's level 4 Frost Queen, and Nia's level 3 Redeeming Strike.
Dragonbane Shot (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using a Bitball. In the , it is also one of Mòrag's arts when using Bunnie.
Eclipse Blade (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Mòrag's arts when using a Chroma Katana.
Dragon Incenses are Ore collectibles in . They can be found in the Kingdom of Uraya, in particular any Collection Point in the Dragon's Stomach.

Dusk Bamboos are Vegetable collectibles in . They can be found in the Empire of Mor Ardain, in particular south of the Old Industrial District on the Upper Level. They are used as an ingredient in Pan-Fried Tartari for Pyra's Cooking and are used to refine Spike Defense II Aux Cores. In the , Dusk Bamboos can also be obtained by scanning an amiibo.
Dynamite Knuckle (Japanese: ) is a Driver Art in . It is one of Zeke's arts when using Knuckle Claws.
Drac Lexos (Japanese: , Ryūzasu Rekusosu) are enemies in . They are members of the Lexos family and can be found at level 43-46 on Baldotas Isle in the Leftherian Archipelago.

Dreadnik Jagrons (Japanese: , Doredoniku Jagāru) are enemies in . They are members of the Jagron family, and can be found at level 42-45 on Godsford Isle in the Leftherian Archipelago.

His father was an officer in the Gormotti army prior to the annexation of the Titan by the Empire of Mor Ardain. He is also a good family friend of Mabon and Vess.
Edgar is an NPC in . Edgar is a Gormotti who can be found in Torigoth in the Gormott Province, outside of the Saets Chief's Residence. He acts as the Chief of Torigoth.
Duwey is an NPC in . Duwey is a Gormotti who can be found at the Torigoth Market in the Gormott Province. Duwey runs the Zelkova Blacksmiths shop, which is specialized in Core Chips.

Effi Krabbles (Japanese: , Ēfi Kuraibu) are enemies in . They are members of the Krabble family, and can be found at level 36-40 after Salvaging at Goetuis Wharf #1 in the Indoline Praetorium.

Dr. Castrofari is an NPC in . He can be found at the Old Factory in the Empire of Mor Ardain during the quest Eternal Spirit. He is the mastermind of the abduction of children to make Artificial Blades from them.

Dress Uniform Mòrag (Japanese: , Shikitenyō Reisō no Merefu) is a DLC Accessory in that increases the wearer's dexterity stat. It grants the same bonus as Legendary rarity Carbon Gloves. Dress Uniform Mòrag cannot be worn with Rainbow Gloves, Carbon Gloves, Hero Gloves, Vivid Mitts, Scarlet Inquisitor Mòrag, or another Dress Uniform Mòrag. When equipped by Mòrag it changes her outward appearance to a white version of her standard uniform, with no hat.
